title: International migration — current-day UN regional snapshot
notes: Net migration tablets use UN World Population Prospects 2024, calendar year 2023 — the last estimate year in that revision (2024–2100 are projections). Net = immigrants minus emigrants. A regional net cancels moves that stay inside the region.
We do not split net into invented 'arrived' and 'left' counts. Annual in- and out-flows are not published as a complete global matrix.
Who-lives-where lists use UN DESA International Migrant Stock 2024 (mid-2024). Stock is not 'arrived this year'.

Country corridors are migrant-stock corridors from IOM World Migration Report 2026 citing UN DESA IMS 2024. They accumulate years of movement. Arrows on the map are schematic only — no invented volumes on the lines.
Intra-regional migration often dominates. Africa→Europe is a real corridor, not the main global story.

netMigration.indicator: Net number of migrants (immigrants minus emigrants)
netMigration.citation: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2024). World Population Prospects 2024. Net number of migrants, both sexes, calendar year 2023, UN M49 major regions.
netMigration.geography: UN M49 major regions (Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, Northern America, Oceania). Northern America is Canada, the United States, Bermuda, Greenland, and Saint Pierre and Miquelon — not Mexico.
netMigration.estimateNote: WPP 2024 treats 1950–2023 as estimates and 2024–2100 as projections. Tablets use 2023 estimates.

migrantStock.citation: United Nations (2025). International Migrant Stock 2024. POP/DB/MIG/Stock/Rev.2024. Destination totals from Key facts and figures annex; origin splits from IOM World Migration Report 2026 chapter 3, citing UN DESA 2025.

intraRegional.note: Shares of people born in a region who live in another country of the same region — not shares of the destination stock, except where IOM states the destination mix.

corridors.note: Largest country-to-country corridor in the IMS 2024 tables. Stock has eased from a 2015 high near 12 million.
Largest inter-regional stock corridor in IMS 2024 key facts.
Gulf labour corridor inside Asia in the IMS 2024 regional grouping. Intra-Asian, not Europe.
Largest Asian country corridor in IOM WMR 2026. Long-standing displacement and residence; not an annual flow.
Second-largest Asian country corridor in 2024 stock. Conflict displacement accumulated over years.
Asian-born residents of Europe. Includes labour, family, and refugee stock — not one route.
IMS 2024 inter-regional corridor. Overlaps Africa and Western Asia; do not read as all of Africa.
African-born residents of Europe. Smaller than intra-African stock (~25 million) and smaller than Asian-born residents of Europe (20 million).
Largest corridor involving African countries in IOM WMR 2026 — long-standing West African labour migration. Volume not restated here as a precise census.
Post-colonial and labour stock. One North Africa–Europe corridor, not the African average.
IOM ranks this among Africa's larger extra-regional corridors. Stock, not 2024 arrivals.
Rose from about 270,000 in 2020 after the 2022 full-scale invasion. Intra-European displacement stock.
UNHCR/IOM: most Venezuelans in need of protection in Colombia. Intra-regional — not the Mexico–United States corridor.
Second intra-LAC Venezuelan corridor named by IOM. Eight of the region's ten largest country corridors still end in the United States.
Largest corridor involving Oceania. Stable over decades.
Second-largest Oceania corridor in IOM WMR 2026.
Only intra-Oceania corridor in IOM's Oceania top five.
Asian-born residents of Northern America. IMS also lists Eastern and South-Eastern Asia → Northern America at 12 million as a sub-corridor.
